chunks: It is narrated from Abī al-Rabīʿ al-Shāmī, who said:
We were with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and the house was crowded with its people.

He said: “He is not from us who does not excel in the companionship of the one who accompanies him, the accompanying of the one who travels with him, the courteous fellowship of the one who shares food with him, and good character toward the one who interacts with him.”

key_terms.صُحْبَةَ: companionship and keeping good company with others
key_terms.لَيْسَ مِنَّا: an expression of disavowal from the moral path and conduct of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.مُخَالَقَةَ: showing good character and conduct toward others
key_terms.مُرَافَقَةَ: accompanying someone, especially in travel or close association
key_terms.مُمَالَحَةَ: courteous sociability with one who shares food or table fellowship

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach about good companionship and manners with others?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the importance of حسن المعاشرة and noble conduct in all forms of human companionship, especially during travel and shared living. It presents good companionship, courtesy, and refined character as marks of belonging to the way of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
